card.name: Three of Swords
card.alchemy: The piercing of the heart by truth; the necessary wound

symbols.meaning: The direct wound of truth; the pain that is felt in the core of the self
Tears; the external world mirroring the internal storm

symbols.symbol: Heart still red and beating (in some versions)
symbols.meaning: The wound has not killed; the heart still lives despite the pain

card.interp_upright: The Three of Swords is the card of the broken heart. There is no softening this image: three swords pierce the heart directly. When this card appears, pain is present. A truth has been spoken that cannot be unheard. A betrayal, a loss, a grief â€” it is real, and it hurts. The card does not ask you to rise above it or find the silver lining. It asks you to feel it. The swords of the mind have cut the heart, and the only path through is to let the wound be a wound. Grief is not a problem to solve; it is a passage. Walk through it.
card.interp_reversed: Reversed, the swords are being withdrawn. Healing begins. But beware the trap of premature forgiveness â€” or the numbness that masquerades as recovery. Ask: have I actually felt this grief, or have I simply pushed it down?
card.material_grounding: Cry. Journal. Speak to someone you trust. The Three of Swords gives permission to be broken. There is no action to take today except to honour the hurt.
card.historical_note: The Golden Dawn called this card the Lord of Sorrow. The three swords through the heart evoke the sorrows of Mary â€” the seven wounds of the mother. In alchemy, this is the phase of 'mortificatio' â€” the necessary death of the old self.

card.name: King of Pentacles
card.alchemy: The stone transmuted into gold; the alchemist who has achieved the Great Work

symbols.symbol: King seated on a throne with pentacles adorning his robe and crown, a castle or city behind him
symbols.meaning: The ruler who has built a kingdom through patience and wisdom; his wealth is visible and shared
Taurus â€” the fixed earth; the strength that endures all seasons
The power of command and the resources to execute; the king who can fund his vision
The blood of life and the earth of the body; fully incarnate sovereignty

card.interp_upright: The King of Pentacles is the card of the master builder who now sits on the throne. He has been the Page (student), the Knight (persistent worker), the Queen (nurturer of the world) â€” and now he governs the entire material realm. When this card appears, you are at the apex of your practical powers. Financial stability is present or achievable. Projects succeed. The body is strong. This King does not flaunt his wealth; he uses it to build, to protect, and to give. His authority is earned. Step into your own. There is nothing you cannot manage today.
card.interp_reversed: Reversed, the King becomes the miser or the bankrupt tyrant. Greed corrupts his legacy, or his stubbornness destroys what he built. Ask: am I serving my wealth, or is my wealth serving life?
card.material_grounding: Take full stock of your material situation today â€” net worth, health, possessions. Then make one wise decision about it. The King of Pentacles governs with clarity and generosity; he does not hide from the numbers.
card.historical_note: The Golden Dawn King is the air of earth â€” the intellectual governance of matter. He is Midas, who learned that gold cannot be eaten; and Solomon, who built the Temple. In the Thoth deck, he is the 'King of the Gnomes and the Mountain,' lord of the depths and the heights of material existence.

card.name: The Chariot
card.alchemy: The vehicle of the soul; the disciplined containment of opposing forces

symbols.meaning: Opposing forces â€” conscious/unconscious, light/dark â€” yoked together and pulling forward
The alchemical square; the four elements, grounding
The world left behind in pursuit of the goal; the conquest that departs from comfort
The Charioteer steers by will alone, not by force

card.interp_upright: The Chariot is the card of the will made visible. The Charioteer does not fight his sphinxes â€” he yokes them. The light and the dark within him both pull the vehicle forward. This is not the peaceful balance of Temperance; this is the tense, disciplined harnessing of contradictions. When this card appears, you are being asked to take the reins of your own life with fierce intentionality. Victory is possible, but only if you stop letting your moods dictate your direction. The work now is to move â€” not when you feel ready, but because you have decided.
card.interp_reversed: Reversed, the Chariot crashes. The sphinxes pull in opposite directions. The will has scattered; projects stall; momentum is lost. There may be a humiliation â€” a public failure, a loss of face. The question becomes: where did I lose the grip? And what must I release in order to regain it?
card.material_grounding: The Chariot asks: what is the one thing you are being asked to complete right now? Not ten things. One. The project that has been drifting. The commitment you made and half-kept. Gather the scattered pieces, set a deadline, and move. The engine is waiting.
card.historical_note: In the Marseille deck, Le Chariot is a warrior in a square vehicle pulled by two horses â€” often coloured red and blue. The square body is the quaternary of the elements; the horses are the warring passions, domesticated only by constant attention.

full_reading:
Querent, let us proceed with the reading. The cards have chosen to reveal themselves to you today.

In the past, we find the Three of Swords. This card is a direct wound to the heart. A truth has been spoken that cannot be unheard. You have experienced heartbreak, sorrow, painful truth, betrayal, or grief. These wounds run deep and are not easily forgotten. They are an echo within you still.

In the present, we find the King of Pentacles. This card is a master builder who sits on the throne. He has reached the apex of his practical powers, governing the entire material realm with clarity and generosity. His authority is earned, and he uses his wealth to build, protect, and give. Your current situation is one of financial stability, project success, and physical strength.

And in the future, we find The Chariot. This card is a vehicle for the soul, where opposing forces are yoked together and pulled forward by sheer willpower. You are being asked to take control of your life with fierce intentionality, stopping the moods that dictate your direction. Victory is possible if you can harness your contradictions.

Now look here: The thread that binds these cards is a paradoxical truth. Your greatest strength lies in your willingness to feel pain and vulnerability, as seen in the Three of Swords. But this same openness to hurt also makes you susceptible to being controlled by emotions, which is exactly what The Chariot is trying to free you from. This tension between feeling deeply and being driven by willpower is a crucial balance you must maintain.

Here is the turn: Your current position of material mastery (King of Pentacles) can either serve as a foundation for your growth or become a prison that stifles it. The question is, are you using your wealth to build and give, or are you serving it instead of life?

The cards are not finished with you yet.

Now look at the present moment: You have the power to choose how you wield your material success. Will you be like the King of Pentacles, governing with clarity and generosity, or will you let greed corrupt your legacy? The decision is yours.

The cards have spoken. One thing stands before you tomorrow:

Tomorrow, take a clear-eyed inventory of your material situation. Write down every asset, liability, and debt. Then make one wise decision about how to manage it, aligning with the values of generosity and stewardship embodied by the King of Pentacles.
